einzeiler: Two wrongful conviction cases reveal how flawed witness testimony destroys innocent lives.
kurzfassung: This episode investigates two wrongful conviction cases built on questionable witness testimony and lacking physical evidence. Gloria Killian spent over sixteen years in prison for a murder she did not commit before a federal appeals court set aside her conviction due to prosecutorial misconduct. Similarly, Clarence Elkins was imprisoned for life based largely on his six-year-old niece's testimony before new DNA evidence eventually cleared him years later.
stichpunkte: Gloria Killian was convicted in 1981 of masterminding a robbery homicide, largely based on testimony from career criminal Gary Massey.
While behind bars, Killian became a jailhouse attorney, helping several women overturn their sentences or win clemency.
Decades later, a legal team uncovered letters showing the prosecutor had recommended leniency for Massey and failed to disclose it.
The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals denounced the prosecution's conduct and ordered Killian's release after 16 years in prison.
Clarence Elkins was convicted in 1998 of murdering his mother-in-law based almost entirely on the testimony of his six-year-old niece.
Private investigator Martin Yant and Elkins' defense team uncovered overlooked evidence and pointed to an alternative suspect who resembled Elkins.
The key eyewitness later recanted her testimony, stating she was never entirely sure the intruder was her uncle.
Clarence Elkins was ultimately exonerated and released after DNA evidence linked a neighbor to the crime.

beschreibung:
Are they guilty of terrible crimes or are they victims themselves?  "48 Hours" examines two separate reports: Gloria Killian, who was arrested for a robbery-homicide she claimed she did not commit, and Clarence Elkins, who was incarcerated for the murder of his mother-in-law but maintained his innocence. "48 Hours" correspondents Peter Van Sant and Susan Spencer report.
This classic "48 Hours" episode last aired on 9/13/2003. Watch all-new episodes of “48 Hours” on Saturdays and stream on demand on Paramount+.
